title: Installable PWA app shell for phones
when: The user wants a phone friendly web app that installs to the home screen, opens standalone and paints its frame before any data arrives.
prompt:
Goal: A static app shell (header, content slot, bottom bar) that paints instantly from cache, runs standalone from the home screen and fills in content afterwards.
Steps:
1. index.html holds only the frame: viewport meta with viewport-fit=cover, <link rel="manifest" href="manifest.webmanifest">, <header>, <main id="view"> and a <nav> bar.
2. Inline the frame CSS (under 10 KB) so first paint needs no extra request; load app.js as a module.
3. app.js draws a skeleton in #view, fills it from IndexedDB, then refreshes from the network.
4. sw.js precaches only the shell files (index.html, app.css, app.js, icons) so a cold start in airplane mode still shows the frame.
5. Detect standalone with matchMedia("(display-mode: standalone)").matches and hide the "add to home screen" hint there.
6. Route on the client (hash or history API) so every deep path is answered by the same shell.
Quality bar:
- The frame is visible in under 1 second on a mid range phone after the first visit.
- The content slot shows a skeleton, never a blank white screen.
Pitfalls:
- Listing user data in the precache, which then goes stale forever.
- A full screen spinner hiding the frame until the API answers.
- Standalone mode has no browser back button; the shell needs its own.
Verify:
- [ ] The manifest is linked and has display standalone.
- [ ] A service worker is registered and precaches the shell files.
- [ ] The viewport meta includes viewport-fit=cover.
Output: index.html, app.css, app.js, sw.js and manifest.webmanifest.

examples.input: quero que meu app web abra como aplicativo no celular, mesmo sem internet
examples.output: Shell with header, #view skeleton and bottom nav, precached by sw.js, standalone manifest
